caption:
AI just engineered a $31 million, 190-room hotel in 9 days, handling the MEP engineering, electrical systems, plumbing, ductwork and fire suppression coordination that normally takes weeks.

The team connected Kimi K3, a 2.8 trillion parameter AI model, directly to its building design software using MCP, the Model Context Protocol.

Instead of manually modelling every pipe, wire and duct, engineers could describe the requirements in plain English. The AI analysed the blueprints and technical requirements, then built the coordinated building model directly inside the design software.

Traditional workflow: 3 engineers, around 6 weeks, approximately $47,000.

AI-powered workflow: 1 engineer reviewing the output, 9 days, approximately $10,500.

But the biggest opportunity isn't just faster AI engineering or lower construction design costs.

It is clash detection.

In large construction projects, MEP clashes between plumbing, HVAC systems, electrical wiring, structural beams and fire protection systems can lead to expensive change orders once construction has already started.

By using AI-powered MEP engineering, BIM-style coordination, automated clash detection and generative AI for construction design before work begins on-site, teams could potentially reduce costly construction mistakes and rework.

This is where AI in architecture, AI in engineering and AI in construction starts becoming much more interesting.

The engineer doesn't necessarily disappear.

The engineer moves from manually producing every element of the model to reviewing, validating and approving AI-generated engineering work.

Kimi K3. MCP. Model Context Protocol. AI engineering. MEP engineering. Construction technology. Building design automation. AI-powered construction. Generative AI for engineering.

These aren't just AI demos anymore. They're beginning to enter real-world construction workflows.
